hero.label: Made for Ergo
hero.headline: I want to be the person who keeps Ergo running.
hero.subheadline: Ergo is solving a real problem I lived firsthand as a BDR: reps waste hours on CRM updates instead of selling. I want to help build the internal systems that let Ergo scale as fast as its product does. Being the first dedicated operations hire at a YC company reporting directly to Yash and Ishan is exactly the kind of zero-to-one challenge I am looking for.

whyCompany.title: Ergo's product solves the exact pain BDRs feel every day
whyCompany.body: I spent over a year as a BDR at Copygen.ai manually logging calls, updating HubSpot, and chasing follow-ups. Ergo automates all of that by pulling structured data straight from conversations. I understand the problem from the inside, which means I can communicate it, test it, and help customers get value from it faster.

whyCompany.title: First ops hire at a YC W25 company with zero employees yet
whyCompany.body: Ergo was founded in 2025 and is still in its earliest days, which means the first operations person will have a direct hand in shaping how the company runs. That is not a support role, it is a foundational one. The chance to build processes from scratch alongside founders who previously built Breezy Medical and won Stanford's Hackathon does not come around often.

whyCompany.title: BDR outreach plus digital marketing research connects directly here
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach sequences, managed HubSpot pipelines, and helped close 15 to 20 paying clients, so I know what revenue operations look like from the ground floor. At NextAfter I studied how B2B organizations convert attention into action through data-driven campaigns. Both experiences trained me to think about process, measurement, and what actually moves deals forward.

quote: I have been on the other side of the problem Ergo is solving, and I know exactly how much time and revenue gets lost when your tools can not keep up with your team. I want to be the person who makes sure Ergo's own house is running tight while Yash and Ishan focus on building the product.
